card.name: Words just before a noun in clinical phrases
card.fires_on: Small modifier or linking words that sit right before a specific noun, such as 'a' before vitrector, 'high' before -risk, 'iris' before hooks or dilator rings. Found in drug-label warnings and surgical or anesthesia instructions.

modes.label: Modifier before -risk or lipid
modes.description: An adjective or number sign that leads into a noun phrase like high-risk patients or soybean oil.

modes.label: Surgical tool phrases
modes.description: The word 'a' or 'iris' just before a named eye-surgery instrument.
modes.example: Clear any vitreous prolapse present within or around the scleral wound using<< a>> vitrector.

modes.label: Anesthesia gas and circuit
modes.description: Partway through sevoflurane, or 'in' before the anesthesia circuit.
modes.example: The exothermic reaction that occurs with se<<v>>oflurane and CO 2
